Afterwards, review questioning with the telephone worker and add a final combined repeat-back of date, time and number. Verify through demonstration and check the next reservation record too.

rst-2-svc-03.summary: Teach accurate information, clear speech and respectful suggestions by example.
rst-2-svc-03.activity: Read for 8 minutes and role-play a telephone reservation for 8 minutes. Create a recommendation explanation in 7 minutes and turn vague phrases into specific guidance in 7 minutes.

rst-2-svc-04.title: Priorities during busy periods and customer information
rst-2-svc-04.objective: Organise competing requests around safety and quality and share customer information appropriately.

paragraphTitles.knowledge: Observe the whole operation and assign help

paragraphs.knowledge: When routine tasks overlap, prioritise serving finished food and adjust payment, seating and orders to circumstances. Safety incidents such as accidents or sudden illness are a separate priority. Acknowledge customers and explain waits while the manager allocates help according to kitchen and dining-area bottlenecks.
paragraphs.procedure: Add thanks when greeting returning guests and share seating and food preferences only as needed. Define personal-data purposes, access rights and storage and prevent unattended papers or devices. If food is delayed, verify the reason and expected timing and coordinate customer explanations with staffing.
paragraphs.mistakes: Do not apply priorities mechanically: a collapsed customer in a passage takes precedence over ready hot food. Do not leave paying customers waiting without acknowledgment or discuss a regular’s preferences or address where other customers can hear. Prevent copying customer data to personal devices or using it for other purposes.
paragraphs.scenario: Food for three tables is ready while customers wait at the till and entrance. The supervisor assigns one worker to serving and personally acknowledges and handles payment. Explain the wait at the entrance and seat guests once a table is ready. Afterwards, record where congestion began and review the next staffing plan.

rst-2-svc-04.summary: Prioritise safety, deploy people according to quality and waits, and keep customer-data handling to the minimum necessary.
rst-2-svc-04.activity: Read for 8 minutes and prioritise a situation with five simultaneous requests in 8 minutes. Practise explanations for 7 minutes and explain appropriate personal-data sharing in 7 minutes.

rst-2-svc-05.title: Answer questions about dietary restrictions and date limits
rst-2-svc-05.objective: Check ingredient, equipment and date conditions and explain in light of dietary wishes and safety.

paragraphTitles.mistakes: Dish names and heating alone do not guarantee suitability

paragraphs.knowledge: Food allergies, religious restrictions and vegetarian diets differ, and avoided ingredients and acceptable limits vary by person. Check sauces, stocks, seasonings and shared pots and utensils. For alcohol, follow laws and restaurant procedures for age and driving checks and consistently explain refusals where service is prohibited.
paragraphs.procedure: Use-by dates concern safety, while best-before dates concern quality retention; both assume unopened storage according to the stated method. After opening, follow the restaurant’s conditions and use period. The manager checks dates, storage and opening records together and does not independently serve expired products.
paragraphs.mistakes: Do not assume heating an alcohol-containing seasoning necessarily meets a customer’s wishes. Vegetarian dishes may still contain animal-derived stock or gelatin. Do not dismiss an unusual taste complaint as preference: if spoilage or chemical contamination is possible, do not taste it; stop service and examine processes and ingredients.
paragraphs.scenario: A customer wants to avoid animal ingredients. Before suggesting vegetable soup, the worker checks stock, oil and seasonings with the supervisor. Explain shared utensils too, and state what is verified and what cannot be accommodated. Help the customer decide without vague absolute guarantees.

rst-2-svc-05.summary: Verify dietary restrictions and date limits in concrete terms and provide accurate information for customer decisions.
rst-2-svc-05.activity: Read for 8 minutes and compare date decisions before and after opening in 7 minutes. Practise asking about ingredient restrictions for 8 minutes, then explain alcohol checks and unusual-taste responses in 7 minutes.

rst-2-svc-06.title: Inspect opening, closing and dining-area cleaning
rst-2-svc-06.objective: Set responsibilities and completion standards for preparation, closing and routine cleaning and hand service over safely.

paragraphTitles.mistakes: Do not standardise all dilution ratios or times
paragraphTitles.scenario: The next morning’s worker finds poor preparation

paragraphs.knowledge: Opening work prepares surroundings and staff to welcome guests. Closing work checks food storage, money, fire and security and hands over to the next day. Train cleaning with specific tools, steps, scope, finish and frequency, rather than appearance alone.
paragraphs.procedure: Before opening, check air conditioning, lights, equipment, supplies and attendance and contact absent staff. At closing, coordinate last orders with the kitchen and check remaining food, till differences, heat sources, locks and security systems. Use area-specific tools for tables, chairs, supplies and toilets and separately record daily, weekly and monthly schedules.
paragraphs.mistakes: Do not apply an example dilution ratio from one cleaning manual to another product: follow its label. Demonstrate proper mop and glass-tool use. Do not leave wet floors without warning, and keep customer routes open. Set equipment preheat times according to model and service plans too.
paragraphs.scenario: The closing list says complete, but seasoning containers and chair undersides remain dirty. The supervisor establishes differing understandings of cleaning scope and shows targets and finished examples. Revise the process so the worker repeats cleaning and someone else checks. Provide handover space for the next shift to report shortcomings.

rst-2-svc-06.summary: Align responsibilities, scope, conditions and completion checks for opening, closing and cleaning before handover.
rst-2-svc-06.activity: Read for 8 minutes and make an opening/closing checklist in 8 minutes. Explain cleaning completion standards in 7 minutes and practise reporting absences and cleaning shortcomings to the next shift for 7 minutes.

rst-2-svc-07.title: Manage till differences and sales money
rst-2-svc-07.objective: Reconcile cash and cashless records and handle discrepancies and deposits securely.

paragraphTitles.knowledge: Both shortages and excesses are problems
paragraphTitles.mistakes: Do not fill gaps from your wallet

paragraphs.knowledge: Cash below recorded amounts causes a store loss, while excess may mean errors such as change owed to customers. For cashless cancellations and refunds, check both terminal operation and sales records. Traceable records explaining discrepancies matter more than simply balancing the total.
paragraphs.procedure: Check change preparation and shortage procedures and train new payment methods. After closing, the responsible worker and checker reconcile actual cash, till records, cancellations, refunds and money movements. Stores using a night safe follow security procedures for designated bags, deposit slips and multiple-person checks, and store next-day change separately.
paragraphs.mistakes: Do not conceal shortages with personal money or carry surplus cash to another day. Do not recharge based only on a failed-payment screen: verify transaction status to prevent duplicate payments. Avoid telling unrelated people sales amounts, storage locations or transport times.
paragraphs.scenario: At closing, actual cash exceeds records. The supervisor checks change, cancellations, refunds and interim deposits in order and reports the discrepancy as found. If a change error is identified, follow store procedures and practise error-prone operations with the worker. Do not vaguely carry it over to tomorrow.

rst-2-svc-07.summary: Do not hide discrepancies: investigate causes through records and handle money and payment information according to security procedures.
rst-2-svc-07.activity: Read for 8 minutes and solve a till-record and cash reconciliation example in 8 minutes. Practise duplicate-payment prevention explanations for 7 minutes and organise deposit checks and security procedures in 7 minutes.

rst-2-svc-08.title: Direct initial responses to complaints and emergencies
rst-2-svc-08.objective: Secure health and safety first, record facts, actions and causes separately and prevent recurrence.

paragraphTitles.scenario: A hard fragment is found on a plate

paragraphs.knowledge: Complaints offer clues for service improvement, but foreign objects and illness can directly harm health. The manager first checks the customer’s condition and safety and listens without interruption. Distinguish facts, wishes and the restaurant’s actions without asserting unverified causes. Build a system where staff can report even small complaints.
paragraphs.procedure: Stop serving suspected contaminated dishes and preserve actual items and related information. Check injuries and symptoms and make necessary emergency calls and manager notifications. If consciousness or breathing is abnormal, follow 119 instructions and trained procedures and divide duties such as arranging an AED. Assign other people to secure the area and assist other guests.
paragraphs.mistakes: Remaking food without investigating the contamination route allows recurrence. Do not discard evidence or blame the customer. Avoid independent actions such as forcing an unwell person to stand or giving food or drink. Do not make medical judgements: follow emergency instructions. After the initial response, share causes and countermeasures with all staff.
paragraphs.scenario: A guest reports something unusual in their mouth and a hard fragment is found. The supervisor checks for injury and arranges preservation of food and fragment. Hold other dishes prepared with the same utensils and inspect for chips. Explain to the guest, make necessary contacts and keep response records. Once the cause is known, revise utensil-check timing and replacement criteria.

rst-2-svc-08.summary: Secure safety and make necessary calls first, then preserve items and records and verify causes and countermeasures.
rst-2-svc-08.activity: Read for 8 minutes and practise listening to a complaint for 7 minutes. Make role assignments for finding a foreign object in 8 minutes and explain 119 calling and AED arrangements for sudden illness in 7 minutes.

rst-2-ops-01.title: Shift-leader decisions and reporting
rst-2-ops-01.objective: Confirm authority and run planning, execution, evaluation and improvement while maintaining QSCA and hospitality.

paragraphTitles.mistakes: Do not chase profit as a single number
paragraphTitles.scenario: Equipment fails in the manager’s absence

paragraphs.knowledge: Shift leaders maintain quality, service and cleanliness during their assigned period and coordinate staffing, stock, costs and customer responses. Confirm the restaurant’s decision limits and matters to report to the manager. Along with QSCA, concern for others’ happiness and difficulties should extend to coworkers as well as customers.
paragraphs.procedure: Plan from sales forecasts and issues, assign staff and tasks and execute. Observe quality and waiting times during service, then compare results and adjust afterwards. Connect yearly, monthly, weekly and daily plans. Reports to superiors include abnormalities, actions, unresolved matters and requests for the next shift as well as results.
paragraphs.mistakes: Short-term cost reductions from staffing cuts cannot sustain operations if poor service or accidents lose customers. Avoid taking everything on yourself or independently making changes beyond your authority. Base performance appraisal on concrete results, abilities and work behaviour rather than impressions alone.
paragraphs.scenario: Equipment fails while the manager is away. The shift leader stops use for safety and identifies dishes still available. Make staffing changes within your authority and seek manager approval for repair costs or service changes. Tell the next shift the faulty part, prohibited-use area and arrangements and request reopening checks.

rst-2-ops-01.summary: Understand your authority and connect planning, workplace observation, reporting and improvement.
rst-2-ops-01.activity: Read for 8 minutes and organise shift-leader decision limits in 7 minutes. Create a service-change report in 8 minutes and decide next-day verification points in 7 minutes.

rst-2-ops-02.title: Interpret sales and labour-hour indicators
rst-2-ops-02.objective: Calculate indicators from sales, customers, gross profit and total working hours and explain their different meanings.

paragraphTitles.mistakes: Do not confuse sales and gross profit

paragraphs.knowledge: Sales equal customer count × spending per customer; gross profit equals sales − cost of goods. Labour-hours are all employees’ actual working hours added together. Sales per labour-hour = sales ÷ total working hours; customers per labour-hour = customer count ÷ total working hours; labour-hour productivity = gross profit ÷ total working hours. Compare identical periods and conditions, including tax treatment.
paragraphs.procedure: For practice, use sales of 180,000 yen, 150 customers, costs of 54,000 yen and 36 total working hours. Spending per customer is 1,200 yen, gross profit 126,000 yen, sales per labour-hour 5,000 yen and labour-hour productivity 3,500 yen. Customers per labour-hour are about 4.17, rounded to two decimal places. Spending per customer and customers per labour-hour also let you verify sales per labour-hour.
paragraphs.mistakes: Even with equal sales per labour-hour, greater food loss lowers gross profit and labour-hour productivity. The labour distribution ratio is labour costs ÷ gross profit × 100, unlike the labour cost ratio whose denominator is sales. Set targets according to business type and restaurant plans; do not treat reference figures as universal obligations or wage standards.
paragraphs.scenario: Two stores have equal sales, but one has lower gross profit. Before reducing staff numbers, the supervisor checks costs, waste and product mix. Also examine service productivity and waits and choose improvements that reduce loss while maintaining sales. Do not use indicators solely to rush workers.

rst-2-ops-02.summary: Distinguish denominators and units and evaluate sales, gross profit and service together.
rst-2-ops-02.activity: Read for 8 minutes and recalculate the example in 8 minutes. Compare indicators when costs change for 7 minutes and explain the difference between labour distribution and labour cost ratios in 7 minutes.

rst-1-week01-q01.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-1-week01-q01.stem: A staple has come loose near a dish. Which hazard should you consider?
options: Bacterial growth only
Insufficient sugar
Metal fragments entering the food
Loss of vitamins
rst-1-week01-q01.explanation: Metal fragments are a physical hazard that can cause injury if they enter food. Check nearby food and locate the staple, then report it.

rst-1-week01-q02.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-1-week01-q02.stem: What is the problem with using raw-meat tongs to plate cooked meat too?
options: They may transfer bacteria to cooked food
The meat’s weight will always increase
The plating temperature will always drop
All fat will melt
rst-1-week01-q02.explanation: Even if heating reduces bacteria, raw-meat utensils can contaminate the food again. Use separate utensils for each purpose.

rst-1-week01-q03.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-1-week01-q03.stem: What is the main purpose of taking cold ingredients out in small batches while working?
options: To leave them at room temperature for longer
To make packaging easier to tear
To extend the use-by date
To shorten the time outside cold temperature control
rst-1-week01-q03.explanation: Taking out only what is needed reduces time left at room temperature. The purpose is not to extend the date.

rst-1-week01-q04.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-1-week01-q04.stem: Which is appropriate when handling raw chicken to control Campylobacter?
options: Serve it raw without conditions if fresh
Heat thoroughly and prevent contamination of other food
Make heating unnecessary by marinating in seasonings
Serve after only cooling the surface
rst-1-week01-q04.explanation: Campylobacter is a concern in chicken and similar foods. Freshness or seasoning alone cannot guarantee safety.

rst-1-week01-q05.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-1-week01-q05.stem: What should you be aware of when soil attached to rice, beans, or similar ingredients is brought into the kitchen?
options: Food contamination by microorganisms found in nature
All soil is sterile
The presence of soil makes disinfection unnecessary
Soil can be mixed directly into food if dry
rst-1-week01-q05.explanation: Soil can contain microorganisms such as Bacillus cereus. Hygienic control of ingredients and work areas is necessary.

rst-1-week01-q06.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-1-week01-q06.stem: A storage problem is found when receiving red-fleshed fish. Why must you not assume cooking alone solves it?
options: Fish always becomes poisonous when heated
Refrigeration always increases toxins
Some hazards, such as histamine, are not resolved by heating
Soy sauce can always remove the hazard
rst-1-week01-q06.explanation: Effective measures vary by hazard. Do not accept a hazard from improper storage simply because cooking is planned.

rst-1-week01-q07.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-1-week01-q07.stem: The product name and quantity match the delivery note. What check is needed next?
options: Finish receiving inspection without opening anything if the quantity matches
Quality, including packaging, dates and storage conditions
Recheck only the prices on the delivery note
Skip checking the temperature if the delivery address is correct
rst-1-week01-q07.explanation: Receiving inspection requires checking the actual product’s quality and storage conditions as well as matching the paperwork.

rst-1-week01-q08.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-1-week01-q08.stem: An ingredient arrives with an unreadable date label. What is the appropriate action?
options: Copy the date from the same product
Write the receiving date as the expiry date
Remove the packaging and discard the date label
Confirm with the person in charge or supplier before deciding acceptance
rst-1-week01-q08.explanation: Do not leave an unconfirmed date unresolved or label it by guesswork. Obtain accurate information.

rst-2-week01-q01.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-2-week01-q01.stem: A hygiene plan was stamped “checked” before the work began. What corrective action should the person in charge take?
options: Make advance stamping the official method
Treat additional stamps as proof of safety
Teach checking and recording at the time of the actual work and verify what happens
Remove the forms and rely only on verbal promises
rst-2-week01-q01.explanation: Records must be based on actual checks. Stamping in advance makes it impossible to establish whether control was carried out.

rst-2-week01-q02.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-2-week01-q02.stem: More cleaning tools were added, but they are not separated by area and are shared with contaminated areas. What is the improvement?
options: Separate purposes and storage locations and train staff to use the tools accordingly
Use the same tools in a different order
Increase only the number of tools again
Do not separate them until dirt becomes visible
rst-2-week01-q02.explanation: Clarify purposes, storage, and treatment after use, not just the number of tools, to prevent contamination across areas.

rst-2-week01-q03.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-2-week01-q03.stem: A worker wants to replace a grease-cleaning product with an acidic cleaner without authorization. What is the appropriate judgment?
options: Assume all cleaners have the same effect
Choose the one with a strong smell
Mix chemicals to increase the effect
Choose after checking the dirt, material, and product’s intended use
rst-2-week01-q03.explanation: Use cleaners according to the nature of the dirt, utensil material, and product label. Mixing on your own judgment is dangerous.

rst-2-week01-q04.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-2-week01-q04.stem: Detergent and disinfectant are being transferred into beverage bottles. What should the person in charge do?
options: Allow it if staff remember the colors
Correct this by using labelled, dedicated containers that prevent accidental drinking and misuse
Put them in the food refrigerator to distinguish them
Remove labels to make their appearance uniform
rst-2-week01-q04.explanation: Manage chemicals with containers, labels, and storage locations that prevent confusion with food. Do not rely on verbal memory alone.

rst-2-week01-q05.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-2-week01-q05.stem: Disinfected utensils are being returned to a shelf with dirty hands. Which improvement takes priority?
options: Review hygienic handling and storage after disinfection
Unconditionally increase only the chemical concentration
Change only the shelf’s appearance
Only add more records of disinfection time
rst-2-week01-q05.explanation: Cleanliness cannot be maintained if recontamination occurs after disinfection. Manage removal, hands, and storage locations together.

rst-2-week01-q06.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-2-week01-q06.stem: Items placed in the handwashing area have made it unusable. What is appropriate facility management?
options: Allow staff to wipe hands at another counter
Skip handwashing until the items are removed
Restore immediate usability and include it in daily checks
Hide the handwashing-area sign
rst-2-week01-q06.explanation: Handwashing facilities must be usable when needed. Include obstructions and missing supplies in inspections too.

rst-2-week01-q07.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-2-week01-q07.stem: A worker returned a thermometer that failed calibration to its original place. What prevents reuse?
options: Have just one person remember it is faulty
Identify it as unusable, isolate it, and manage a replacement
Replace the display with a normal reading
Change only its storage location every day
rst-2-week01-q07.explanation: Identification and isolation are needed to keep failed instruments out of use, together with a reliable replacement.

rst-2-week01-q08.objective: Apply the hygiene knowledge from week 1 according to the situation.
rst-2-week01-q08.stem: A report says the water has an unusual color. What should the person in charge decide first?
options: Keep using it for cooking if the color is faint
Hide the color with seasoning
Do not record it until the abnormality disappears
Stop using it and investigate the cause and affected scope
rst-2-week01-q08.explanation: Abnormal water affects food and washing too. Do not hide its appearance; suspend use until safety is confirmed.
